To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
flavan- 3-ols and related oligomers (proanthocyanidins) can protect DNA from oxidative damage at concentrations that can occur physiologically.
the flavan-3ols and related procyanidin oligomers are efficient antioxidants in DNA, with a potency similar to that of alpha-tocoherol, ascorbate and glutathione.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential of flavan- 3-ols and related procyanidin oligomers to protect DNA from oxidative damage induced by UVC radiation.
the identification and characterization of the chemical components of foods that may have the potential of preventing the formation of DNA adducts and other DNA damage.
the identification of the mechanisms involved in the protection of DNA against UVC-induced oxidation by flavan- 3-ols and related oligomers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the flavan-3ols and their related oligomeric procyanidins have the capacity to inhibit DNA damage in vitro.
epicatechin, but not catechin, is a potent antioxidant that can protect DNA from UVC-mediated oxidation.
epicatechin, catechin, and procyanidin fractions are efficient in inhibiting the UVC-mediated production of oxo(8)-dG in DNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
epicatechin and procyanidin oligomers are potent antioxidants that can inhibit DNA oxidation.

epicatechin is more efficient than catechins in protecting DNA from oxidative stress, and that the oligomerization of epicatechin is not as important for its antioxidant activity in isolated DNA as it is in cell culture.
the flavan-3ols and procyanindins from cocoa are effective inhibitors of DNA oxidation and that their antioxidant properties are related to their chemical structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
epicatechin and procyanidin fractions can protect DNA from UVC-induced oxidative damage.
flavan- 3-ols and related procyanidin fractions can inhibit the formation of 8-hydroxy-7,8- dihydro-2'-deoxguanosine in DNA.
flavan- 3-ols and related procyanidin oligomers have the capacity to inhibit the formation of oxo(8)dg in isolated DNA.
